# Find a Park

Residents browse local parks on a map, in a list, and on a detail page. This is a front-end proof of concept: the parks live in a static JSON file, and the app runs in the browser.

## Run

Node.js `^20.19.0` or `>=22.12.0` (the range Vite 8 declares).

```bash
npm install
npm run dev
```

Vite prints a local URL, typically http://localhost:5173. No environment variables.

| Script | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `npm test` | Vitest, one run |
| `npm run lint` | ESLint |
| `npm run build` | `tsc -b`, then a production build |
| `npm run preview` | Serves that production build |

## What works

- **Home (`/`).** Every park is in the list. Parks with coordinates are on the map. Below the `md` breakpoint (768px), the header is "Find a Park", the list is on screen, and **Open map** switches to a full-screen map with **Show list**. From `md` up, the map fills the viewport and the list scrolls in a panel on the left.
- **Detail (`/park/:id`).** Name, address, description, amenities, hours, photos, acreage, and rating. A missing description reads "No description available". A missing rating reads "No rating yet". A missing address or acreage omits that row. An unknown id shows "Park not found" and a link home.
- **Search.** A text query matches park name, address, and amenity label, and it filters the list and the markers together. The query is the `q` parameter on the home URL, so Back from a detail page keeps it. While a query is active the heading counts matches, for example "Find a Park (4 of 12)". No matches shows "No parks match" and a clear action.
- **Keyboard.** Each list row is a link. Tab to a park and press Enter to open its details. Interactive controls use a visible focus ring (`ring-2 ring-primary ring-offset-2`).
- **Without a location.** The map does not ask for the resident's position. A park with no coordinates stays in the list and is left off the map.
- **Photos.** Each image goes through `ParkImage`. An empty list or a URL that fails to load shows a placeholder.

## What was left out

The time budget is 2 hours, so the app stays inside the must-haves.

- Backend, accounts, and deployment.
- Geolocation, distance, and any "near me" ordering.
- Filters beyond that one text query.
- Browser end-to-end tests. The tests are Vitest and React Testing Library.
- Local copies of the photos. Images are hotlinked.

## Key decisions

- **Stack.** Vite, React 19, TypeScript (strict), Tailwind CSS v4 (`@tailwindcss/vite`, tokens in `src/index.css`), React Router, react-leaflet with OpenStreetMap tiles, Vitest, and React Testing Library.
- **No API keys.** Tiles come from the public OpenStreetMap tile server. Photos are direct Wikimedia Commons thumbnail URLs.
- **Circle markers.** Each park is a Leaflet `CircleMarker` in the primary blue. That avoids shipping and pathing the default Leaflet marker image.
- **Search state in the URL.** The home page reads and writes `?q=`. `filterParks` runs on that string, and the same filtered array is passed to the list and to `ParkMap`.
- **Icons.** Every icon is from `lucide-react`.
- **Normalize once.** Components do not import `src/data/parks.json`. `src/data/parks.ts` calls `normalizeParks` once, when the module loads, and sorts by name. `getParks()` and `getParkById()` return that result. In `Park`, every field is `T | null`. Missing, blank, or mistyped values become `null`.

## Data changes

`src/data/parks.json` is a copy of `assets/parks.sample.json` with each `images` array replaced by hotlinked Wikimedia Commons photos. The URLs are the 1280px `upload.wikimedia.org` thumbnail form, with any `utm_*` query string removed. `assets/parks.sample.json` is unchanged, and no field other than `images` was edited.

Only Prospect Park is a real park, and its photo is of Prospect Park. The other parks are fictional. Each of them uses a Commons photo chosen to match the park's character (a garden, a marsh, a skate spot, a ball field, and so on). Those photos are stand-ins of other real places.

`highland-dog-park` is intentionally `"images": []`, so the empty-photo case is real data. The placeholder still renders for that park.

## Image credits

File, author, license, and link, copied from the W1.T1 notes in `progress.md`. The link is the thumbnail the app requests. "Depicts" is the real subject of the file, from those same notes and the image-sourcing list in `PLAN.md`.

Highland Dog Park has no photo. That empty `images` array is intentional.

## Known issues

- Hotlinked images depend on Wikimedia. If Commons is unreachable, rate-limits the request, or moves a file, the photo fails and `ParkImage` shows the placeholder. There is no local copy.
- The public OpenStreetMap tile servers are appropriate for this exercise. A public launch needs a tile host that allows the traffic.
- Markers take a pointer click. The keyboard path to a park is the list.
- Three listings are incomplete in the data, and the UI says so: Highland Dog Park has no address and no photos, Old Mill Botanical Garden has no description, and Cedar Hill Nature Preserve has no rating.

## How it was checked

- Every thumbnail above was requested with `curl -sI` and a User-Agent set (Wikimedia rejects a bare HEAD). Each returned HTTP 200. That check is recorded in the W1.T1 block of `progress.md`.
- Unit tests cover `normalizeParks` and the format helpers (`src/data/parks.test.ts`), the detail page with the known missing fields and a failed image (`src/pages/ParkDetailPage.test.tsx`), and `filterParks` (`src/lib/filterParks.test.ts`). The plan runs those tests once, in W5.T1, so this track did not run them.
- `npm run lint`, `npm test`, `npm run build`, and the manual pass at 375px and 1280px (keyboard only from the list to a detail page and back) belong to W5.T1. Results go in [Verification results](#verification-results).

## Time spent

The exercise is budgeted at 2 hours. The track chats did not record start and stop times, so this draft has no measured duration.

## Next steps before public use

- Finish the W5.T1 verification pass and fix what it finds.
- Host the photos, and replace the stand-ins with photos of the named parks, so a Commons outage does not empty the gallery.
- Show the author and license beside each photo. Several files are CC BY or CC BY-SA, which require attribution.
- Serve map tiles from a host that permits the expected traffic.
- Add an address and photos for Highland Dog Park if that listing should be complete.
- Export every project chat, unedited, into `ai-logs/` (W6.T1) before submission.

## AI conversation logs

Every chat used for this project is kept in `ai-logs/`, unedited. That includes the planning chat, each Wave/Track chat, and each commit chat. The work was split into those Wave/Track prompts. The prompts, and the files each track may edit, are in `PLAN.md`.
